note:
AMENDMENT (pre-grill, from the adversarial review of the idea set). Four changes:
(1) AC-2 PRESUPPOSES AN AC IDENTITY THE FORMAT FORBIDS. 'An AC named in a transferred.scope' — but scope is declared VERBATIM FREE TEXT (journey-format-spec §3; the writer checks only that it is a string, store.ts:1486) while conclusion() matches ACs by a normalised prefix of the full AC text (commands/index.ts:1499-1501). A non-empty check does not make a concatenated verbatim scope parseable, so the close rule cannot credit anything. AMEND: define the scope's internal shape (one AC per line as '<AC-id>: <text verbatim>') so credit is ID-based, or state that the credit is text-prefix based and amend the read to match.
(2) gate-revised IS NEAR-TAUTOLOGICAL IN THE COMPOSITE. F-AC16 fires BECAUSE gate-revised exists (store.ts:1662) and then demands the transferred event the gesture writes anyway; no AC defines what {old,new} means for a half-accept. AMEND: either drop gate-revised from the composite or define exactly what changed and why it is recorded.
(3) THERE IS NO TRANSACTION, SO STATE THE ORDER AND THE RESUME. 'ONE validated act' is 3-5 sequential appends (gate!'s own shape, commands/index.ts:556-576); AC-1's 'zero writes' covers VALIDATION only. A crash mid-composite leaves a partial closure and neither this task nor 12/13 states the ordering it relies on (the transfer must be recorded before the auto-completed close, or check() may flag the node later). AMEND: state the order and the resume rule (a re-run completes the sequence; no transaction is claimed).
(4) THE CROSS-TASK COUPLINGS ARE UNDECLARED. AC-2's 'the record reads this AC moved to <target>' is a CARD change (src/surface — not in this task's targetAreas), and 12/13's AC-4 depends on 12/11's read. AMEND: declare both couplings in the contract.

DELIVERY NOTE (post-implementation, leg 12/12) — how the two pre-grill amendments were settled, and the couplings a reviewer should look for.

(1) SETTLED — THE SCOPE HAS AN INTERNAL SHAPE. The amendment was right: the format declares `scope` VERBATIM free text, and a verbatim blob is not parseable, so AC-2's credit could not work as written. Rather than break the format's verbatim promise, the convention is defined (in `src/store/transfer.ts`, and recorded in journey-format-spec §3): ONE AC PER LINE, the id first — `AC-2: <the criterion, verbatim>`. The TEXT is the record; the ID is what the close credits. The credit is ID-based, so a line naming no AC is legal and credits NOTHING (residual scope that maps to no criterion is an honest record that simply cannot satisfy one), and a typo'd id would silently credit nothing — which is why `transfer-unknown-ac` refuses at write time. claims[] still wins over a transfer for the same AC (the claim match is tried FIRST in conclusion()).

(2) SETTLED — `gate-revised` IS DROPPED FROM THE COMPOSITE. The format gives that event only a `{old,new}` pair of gate NAMES; a half accept leaves the gate `confirm`, so writing it would record a revision with nothing revised AND arm F-AC16 against a fact the `transferred` event already states. The composite is therefore accept + transfer (+ close), nothing more. AC-1's parenthetical offered `gate-revised` as part of the gesture; this is the answer to why it is not there.

(3) THE SUCCESSOR RIDES THE GATE DECISION, NOT A FIFTH KIND. `DecisionPoint.successor` is set on the accept when a `transferred` event follows it. A fifth kind was rejected because a `transferred` event carries no `why` channel of its own: as its own kind it would read NO WHY RECORDED on every half accept while the reason sits one event earlier on the accept. This is what 12/13's AC-4 ('the transfer with its why') reads.

(4) THE ONE HONEST LIMIT OF AC-2. `closeEvidenceBlocker` — the single close predicate shared by `complete!` and the confirm-accept auto-close — does NOT read `unclaimed`, so the auto-close is NOT what the transfer unlocks (verified empirically against the built CLI before writing this). AC-3 forbids changing that predicate, so the transfer's verifiable effects are the `complete!` refusal and the READS (conclusion · brief · card): a moved AC stops being reported as an owed gap and is named as moved, with its successor. The auto-close behaviour is unchanged, deliberately.

(5) NOTICED, NOT FIXED — `src/flow/intents.ts:150`. The `close` intent's `gate-revised` arm writes `gate: 'confirm'` (a bare string), which the store's shape check refuses (`gate` must be `{old,new}`). Latent and untested, outside AC-1..AC-5 and outside this task's targetAreas; flagged here so it is not lost.

(6) COUPLING DECLARED. AC-2's user-visible half is `src/surface` (brief's TRANSFERRED block, the decision line) — 12/13's targetArea, touched here because the AC names the read; the served UI card is left to 12/13. The engine half (`src/store/transfer.ts`, `src/commands`) is this task's.

claims.statement: One gesture: gate! <id> confirm accept <why> --transfer <target> --scope <ACs> validates and writes the accept and the transferred record in a single act. The refusals are named and write nothing (the 9-case table in commands.test.ts compares the events file byte-for-byte after each; transfer.e2e.test.ts proves the same through the real CLI, including the exit codes for a lone flag and an unknown successor).

A transferred AC leaves unclaimed and is credited to its target; complete! stops demanding it and names only the criteria neither claimed nor transferred. The scope convention (AC-n heads the line) is defined once in src/store/transfer.ts and recorded in journey-format-spec section 3; the brief renders TRANSFERRED (moved to a successor, not claimed as met) and says every AC claimed only when it is true.

No new status word, no new event type, no fifth decision kind, no change to the leg aggregate, the leg gate, the distance-to-goal read or the ready set. The comparison test runs one task to the same end twice, half accept versus plain accept, and pins every derived read (the two differ by the transferred event alone). The close predicate closeEvidenceBlocker is untouched: it does not read unclaimed, so the auto-close behaves exactly as before and the transfer changes only the complete! refusal and the reads. gate-revised is deliberately not part of the composite, so F-AC16 is not armed against a half accept.

Order-insensitive and idempotent: a transfer recorded before or after the close satisfies F-AC16 (both orders pinned, and the target-existence rule still bites); a second identical transfer refuses by name with zero writes; a target that is not a spawned task refuses at write time, naming the spawn that would make it legal. The last transfer naming an AC wins, matching the append-only rework reading used for claims.

Full suite green (1054 tests, 54 files) and typecheck clean; the five captured checks are recorded with capture! on this node (npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run build, ann check, ann verify), each bound to the sha it ran against. ann check reads OK on the live journey and ann verify reads clean (0 drifts). No live node and no recorded event was rewritten; the only format change is additive documentation of a convention in journey-format-spec section 3.

findings.text: AC-1 requires the gesture to compose the accept + `gate-revised {old,new}` + `transferred {target, scope}` in one act; the composite writes `submitted`/`confirmed`/`transferred`/`completed` but emits NO `gate-revised` event — the comment at :784-790 explicitly declines to write one, so the composed act is missing the revision half the criterion names.

AC-1 requires refusal with ZERO writes when the why is empty, and the frame's own confirm-accept path must carry it too — the transfer option must not become a bypass. The diff shows the why-check precedes the transfer block in `gateImpl`, but no change is shown to the frame's confirm-accept path, so whether the frame path also refuses a transfer without a why (or carries the why) is unverified from the material.

AC-1 requires the transfer to be refused NAMED with ZERO writes when the target does not exist; the write-time target check reads `this.store.ids()`, which is a snapshot taken at Commands construction — a target spawned between construction and the gate call could be refused as non-existent, or a target deleted after construction could pass. The material does not show whether the store re-reads ids at gate time; I would need the `Store.ids()` implementation at 0284c2a.

AC-2 requires the refusal to name exactly the ACs neither claimed NOR transferred and the record to read 'this AC moved to <target>', never 'this AC was met'. The `complete!` refusal message is updated to say 'neither claimed NOR transferred', but the diff does not show the `brief`/card renderer that must emit 'TRANSFERRED (moved to a successor — not claimed as met)' and 'AC-n → target'; the e2e test asserts those strings but the renderer change is not in the reviewed hunks (only the test asserts it).

AC-2's credit mechanism is present: `scopeAcs` parses one AC per line by id and `transferCredit` maps each moved AC to its last-named target, and `conclusion()` consumes it to move transferred ACs out of `unclaimed` into `transferred` (src/commands/index.ts:2065-2090).

AC-3 is pinned by the comparison test that runs one task to the same end by half accept and by plain accept and asserts every derived read (status, leg, ready, lookBack, distance-to-goal, check, verify, event types minus `transferred`) is identical — the strongest available evidence that no new state or aggregate read moved.

AC-4's order-independence and idempotence are pinned: the transfer-then-complete and complete-then-transfer orders both pass `closureProblems()`, the duplicate transfer refuses by name with zero writes, the other-leg target is allowed, and the self-target refuses — each in the reviewed test hunks.

AC-4 requires 'a second identical transfer on the same node refuses by name'; the duplicate check compares `e.target === target && e.scope === scope` after `target` is trimmed but `scope` is NOT trimmed or normalised before comparison, so a whitespace-different scope would pass as a new transfer — the material does not show whether this is intended; I would need the exact comparison semantics at 0284c2a.

AC-5 requires the existing journey untouched and no history rewrite; the diff shows `.ann/journey/events.jsonl` gained 4 lines and `docs/journey-format-spec.md` gained 1 line — the format-spec change is additive documentation, but the events.jsonl churn is not shown in the diff and its content cannot be verified from the material.

AC-1 requires the CLI to parse `--transfer`/`--scope` and refuse a lone flag with a usage error (exit 2); the diff hunk for `src/surface/handlers.ts` and `src/surface/command-renderers.ts` is cut in the material, so the flag-parsing and the 'go together' usage error are asserted only by the e2e test, not shown in the reviewed bytes.

The successor attribution reads the LAST `transferred` event with index > the accept index, regardless of whether that transfer belongs to the accept or a later unrelated one; a second transfer recorded after an accept but belonging to a subsequent decision would be attributed backwards to the earlier accept — the code comment claims 'a transfer recorded BEFORE the accept belongs to whatever preceded it' but does not guard the forward case.

AC-2's scope convention is pinned: `scopeAcs` reads one AC per line by id, dedupes, ignores prose that merely mentions an AC, and `transferCredit` reads the tail with last-wins semantics and ignores malformed transfers — the shape the close rule depends on.
